subject: CFI Value: Regular estimate vs bootstrapLavaan

messages.author: 19cb4d88d5623ce7
messages.subject: CFI Value: Regular estimate vs bootstrapLavaan
parts:
Dear all,

I am running a model in lavaan, and finding wildly different CFI estimates from regular lavaan and from the bootstrapLavaan function.

summary(mod, fit.measures=TRUE)

** CFI = .989

lavaan::bootstrapLavaan(mod, R = 20, FUN = lavaan::fitMeasures, fit.measures = "cfi")

## 20 CFI values
[1,] 0.6933022
[2,] 0.7799376 [3,] 0.8186162 [4,] 0.7391584 [5,] 0.8133046 [6,] 0.7494424 [7,] 0.7153559 [8,] 0.7701116 [9,] 0.8543743 [10,] 0.7685795 [11,] 0.7328343 [12,] 0.8077487 [13,] 0.7807260 [14,] 0.8034772 [15,] 0.6714574 [16,] 0.7543647 [17,] 0.8206758 [18,] 0.7858366 [19,] 0.7241862 [20,] 0.7530089

Any thoughts on why CFI would be so different across these two settings? I might be missing something obvious.

Thanks!
Rob

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFI Value: Regular estimate vs bootstrapLavaan
parts:
When you first fit your model, try setting baseline=FALSE (see ?lavOptions) so that the baseline model's chi-squared is not saved in the lavaan object's @baseline slot.  The fitMeasures() function should then manually fit the baseline model for each bootstrap sample.

Hi Rob,

maybe I misunderstand your question, but I think this has nothing in common with lavaan. It is simply a feature of the (naive) bootstrap. Bollen and Stine (1992) were the first to point this out, as far as I know: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0049124192021002004

HTH

Christian

I see. Maybe (speculation) this will help:

bootstrapLavaan(your.model, R = 10, FUN = function(object) lavInspect(object, "nobs"))

lavInspect(object, "nobs") asserts that each bootstrap draw has the same sample size. This is rather unlikely with listwise deletion. If this information (and not the true sample size of the bootstrap draw) is used to calculate the fit indices, then this would certainly be a source of bias. But this is definitely unknown to me, the answer should be found in the source code :-)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFI Value: Regular estimate vs bootstrapLavaan
parts: Bollen and Stine (1992) were the first to point this out, as far as I know: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0049124192021002004

But their bootstrap would result in CFI always = 1 because they transform the data to be consistent with H0 of perfect fit.  This article proposes a related transformation that keeps the sample's noncentrality parameter constant across bootstrap samples:

https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2015.1118692

This transformation is implemented in bootstrapLavaan(..., type = "yuan").  But lavaan doesn't apply these transformations with partially observed data, so it only works in combination with missing="listwise".  In that case, the sample size would be constant across bootstrap samples because it copies the data stored in the lavaan object.
> does bootstrapLavaan() use a different method of treating missing data?

All your options are simply copied.  Christian showed how you can check the sample size per bootstrap, but you should also be able to use lavInspect(object, "data") to retrieve each bootstrapped sample.  Perhaps that would be be enlightening.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
